external_narratives.summary: Detailed crew page for Lancaster DV382 (KC-J) of 617 Squadron. The aircraft took off at 08:20 on 12 February 1944 from RAF Ford, where it had landed after an operation against the Antheor Viaduct in southern France. Within five minutes, in low cloud, the Lancaster flew into trees at the top of Littleton Down.
external_narratives.key_details: Crew: S/L William R. Suggitt DFC (Pilot, died of injuries 15 Feb at St Richard's Hospital Chichester), F/S John Pulford DFM (Flight Engineer, Dambuster veteran who flew with W/C Gibson on the Dams Raid May 1943), F/O J.I. Gordon DFC (Navigator), F/O N.J. Davidson (Bomb Aimer), F/O S.G. Hall (WOp/AG), F/S J.P. Riches (Mid Upper AG), F/O J.M. Dempster DFM (Rear AG), S/L T.W. Lloyd DSO (Passenger).
external_narratives.link_description: Detailed crew page for Lancaster DV382 (KC-J) of 617 Squadron's historic mission.

external_narratives.summary: Account of the memorial dedication at Upwaltham where a Lancaster from the Battle of Britain Memorial Flight performed a flyover. The tiny hamlet of 25 inhabitants raised over 10,500 pounds for the memorial stone.
external_narratives.key_details: The hamlet of Upwaltham (population 25) fundraised for the memorial. BBMF Lancaster flyover conducted at the dedication ceremony. F/S Pulford's DFM was gazetted 28 May 1943 for his role in the Dams Raid.
external_narratives.link_description: Witness dedication ceremony and impressive Lancaster flyover at Upwaltham's memorial site.

external_narratives.key_details: Aircraft code KC-J. The crash occurred while departing RAF Ford after an operational landing. S/L Lloyd DSO was a passenger, bringing the total aboard to eight.

memorial_details:
Name: Avro Lancaster DV382
Type: Board / Plaque / Tablet
Description: Incised black stone tablet atop a short raised brick pedestal. Gold inscription text.
Inscription: Badge: SQUADRON/ 617 617/ ROYAL AIR FORCE/ APRES MOI LE DELUGE/ Inscription: THIS IS THE SITE/ WHERE A LANCASTER BOMBER DV382/ 617 DAMBUSTER SQUADRON/ CRASHED ON 13 FEBRUARY 1944/ WITH THE LOSS OF LIFE OF ALL THE CREW./ (Names)/ STRANGER, WHEN PASSING REMEMBER, IF IT WAS NOT/ FOR HEROES LIKE THESE, WE WOULD NOT BE HERE TODAY.
Location: At edge of woodland north of village. North Down Upwaltham Chichester West Sussex GU28 0LY England
Grid Ref: SU 94034 14877
Coordinates: 50.926180246395,-0.662065744400
Photos: https://media.iwm.org.uk/ciim5/memorials/162/487/large_ws_waltham_down_1.jpg; https://media.iwm.org.uk/ciim5/memorials/162/488/large_ws_waltham_down_3.jpg; https://media.iwm.org.uk/ciim5/memorials/162/489/large_ws_waltham_down_4_r.jpg; https://media.iwm.org.uk/ciim5/memorials/168/552/large_106342_jo_brown_november_2023_r.jpg

Memorial Dedication: The memorial is dedicated to the Avro Lancaster DV382 aircraft and its crew.

Unveiling of the memorial (February 1944): Dedication to Dambuster John Pulford and his 617 Squadron crew, killed on their return from an operation.
narrative: Lancaster DV382, coded KC-J and assigned to 617 Squadron, was on an operation when it crashed near Upwaltham in Sussex on 13 February 1944. All eight crew members were killed. Among those lost was John Pulford, a veteran of 617 Squadron's Dambuster raids of the previous year. Flight Sergeant John Paul Riches, the aircraft's air gunner, was 22 years old at the time of his death. Charles Whitworth and Gus Walker also died in the crash. No one aboard survived.

community_connection: The image was created and shared by Waltham Down, indicating a local community involvement in preserving and sharing this historical artifact. The memorial was a result of community efforts, with Dione Venables sending the picture and Sue Kearsey also involved in its creation or maintenance.
